thread.title: SoftBank On A Growth Trajectory - SoftBank Group ADR (OTCMKTS:SFTBY)

author: Harold Goldmeier
title: SoftBank On A Growth Trajectory - SoftBank Group ADR (OTCMKTS:SFTBY)
text:
It is the right time to BUY SoftBank ADR ( OTCPK: SFTBF , OTCPK: SFTBY ). The share price has dipped to $36-$38. The founder and CEO is driven to building SFTBY bigger and more profitable by becoming the premier AI (artificial intelligence) and ML (machine learning) tech investment company. The CEO, once enamored with startups, is shifting attention to late-stage companies and unicorns located all around the world. He made a commitment to employees that they, too, will benefit. That commitment helps ensure stability up and down the line. There are also international considerations and developments that make this a good investment.
The last eighteen months have been a breakout time for SFTBY and the units through which the company invests. The 52-week low was $34.82. The high was $46.56, but as values from companies in which STFBY invests are factored into the equation, going forward, the stock possibly can top $60 per share. In 2014, SFTBY shares popped to near $45 each. The price descent was slow until 2016 when shares touched down into the low $20s. Since then, the price of shares steadily climbed back.
SoftBank's founder and CEO, M. Son, is reputed to be a tough dealmaker and "an unstoppable force in the technology world over the last year." His roster of big backers includes Saudi Arabia's crown prince and Apple's (NASDAQ: AAPL ) Tim Cook as the company rebuilt on a new vision . The Japanese company is considered by analyst Chris Lane to be "evolving into the Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK.A ) (NYSE: BRK.B ) of the tech world." Others are less generous in their praise questioning the sustainability of the "dizzying array" of companies in which SFTBY is investing.
Fundamental conditions and SoftBank technicals seem to be coming together "just right." The Asia initiative by the Trump Administration may bring military peace for a time to the region. This gives Japan's President Abe time to focus on his economic revitalization plan. Moreover, Trump tariff threats are the building blocks of new bilateral relations, according to The Japan Times (April 14, 2018), between China and Japan.
Here are a few recent deals. SoftBank sold its majority holding in a chip design firm to a China-led group of investors at what some consider a bargain price. The sale dramatically boosts China's expansion in the semiconductor market. At this week's SoftBank annual meeting Chief Executive Son announced its India-based OYO Hotels (100K rooms) is expanding into 26 cities (+11K rooms) in China. According to Mr. Son, OYO Hotels is the "next generation hotel company using the Internet service." In a tightly controlled economy, business and tourism expansion requires the hand-in-glove cooperation of China's government.
The China Investment Corporation is China's largest sovereign wealth fund holding $800B. President Trump's tariff proposals are pushing China to invest outside of America and possibly into the waiting arms of SFTBY. CIC and SoftBank supposedly are discussing a substantial investment in Vision Fund tech projects. China is on a tear to become the world's center for AI and ML leadership. SFTBY raised $100B elsewhere, but a financial relationship with CIC will strengthen the Japan-China relationship and help both China and SFTBY achieve their mutual goals.
In my opinion, Mr. Son uses the Vision Fund as a political communications device for Japan to build dialogue and open business opportunities with recalcitrant nations like China, Korea, Malaysia, India, and Israel. Japan was a faithful subscriber for decades to the Arab League boycott of Israel but is investing heavily in Israel-based tech companies and that is softening political hard feelings. Japan has maintained tenuous relations with many countries until recently.
Mr. Son largely looks for investment opportunities in companies and industries that have AI and ML common cores or potential: ride-sharing companies, life sciences, agriculture, cancer detection, self-driving vehicles, satellite startups, robot makers, and more; i.e., the industries and companies Son and Vision Fund are targeting have their futures tethered to AI, ML, and high-tech.
In a Bloomberg interview last year, "Son painted a picture of the future where satellite networks cover every inch of the Earth and a trillion devices connected to the Internet disgorge data into the cloud where it is analyzed by artificial intelligence. SoftBank and its companies will be there at every step of the way, the billionaire said."
A company like WeWork, in which Son invested $300M, appears to have little to do with high-tech but this fifth most valuable startup plans more than 20 locations in Japan. WeWork creates environments, not office space, environments stimulating creativity, information sharing, and innovation. Europe's Airbus SE ADR (OTCPK: OTCPK:EADSY ) rented space in a Tel Aviv WeWork building last month, in order to take advantage of Israel's aerospace and hi-tech R&D.
Let's not forget the investments the company is making in the fast-expanding business of cybersecurity. SFTBY is a partner in creating the first Global Telco Security Alliance offering a comprehensive portfolio of cybersecurity services. The alliance has 1.2B customers in 60 countries. SFTBY made a $100M investment in 2017 in Israel's Cybereason security firm that employs behavioral analytics and ML to process information and analyzes it in real time. Son invested $120M in Israeli startup Lemonade Insurance that relies on AI and behavioral economics selling insurance now in eight US states.
Mr. Son talks about his 300 years vision, but even at the early age of 60 pundits raise worries about SFTBY's future without him. He talks about stepping down from managing the company he founded in 1981 sometime in the next ten years. Not to worry. It was announced on June 20th that two executives were promoted and one brought in from the outside to Son's inner circle (a Brazilian, an Indian and Japanese). Bringing a female into the inner circle would have enhanced confidence in management's commitment to a diversified perspective.
SoftBank's debt is manageable and bond sales, though slow among institutions lately, bond sales are vibrant among individual investors. Son argues that analysts worrying about SFTBY debt accumulation do not adequately consider the rise in the value of the investments he has made. For instance, an investment of $20M in 2000 in the Alibaba Group Holding Ltd (NYSE: BABA ) skyrocketed to an estimated value in 2018 of about $129B. Bloomberg's default risk model indicates the risk of SoftBank defaulting this year on its debt is half of what it was in 2016.
SFTBY has been investing in startups that take years if ever to yield value and profits. Though predictions are strong with some forecasting a target price topping $64 per share, many welcome Mr. Son's intentions of investing in late-stage companies and unicorns to hasten the pace of a better ROI.
SoftBank is a good investment. The share price has been near its 52-week low. The founder and CEO, M. Son, is active on a daily basis in the business. He has a vision, the drive and a feel for a good tech investment. Softbank is buying into the future with investments in tech, ML and AI companies that will dominate work, service industries, production, intellectual property, medicine and life sciences, manufacturing, and distribution. The CEO plans to focus on adding value faster to STFBY targeting companies with proof of concept.
